$comment: Manifest of upstream fixes we are waiting on, each tied to a local
workaround in this repo. The track-upstream-fixes.yaml workflow runs
check-upstream-fixes.sh against every entry and flags (opens/updates a
GitHub issue) when a fix has landed in a way that lets us revert the
workaround.
Each entry supports one of these check types:
release-contains-commit:
Resolved when the repo's LATEST release tag's commit is a descendant
of (or equal to) `fix_commit`. Best for 'fix merged to main but not
yet released' situations -- which is exactly the gh-dash case.
release-min-version:
Resolved when the repo's latest release tag (semver) is >= `min_version`.
Use when upstream tells you the fix ships in a named release.
issue-closed:
Resolved when the tracked issue is in the closed state. Weakest signal
(an issue can close before a release ships) -- prefer the two above.
pkgs-min-version:
Channel-aware. Resolved only when the version of `package` as it
resolves in THIS repo's pinned nixpkgs (evaluated via the flake on
`eval_host`) is >= `min_version`. This is the only honest signal for
'the fix is installable in a channel we actually build' -- a merged
PR or a closed issue does NOT mean it has landed in our pin. Use this
for nix/nixpkgs-daemon-level fixes. `min_version` may be null when a
fix is known to be coming but the carrying release is not yet known;
the entry then stays BLOCKED (never falsely resolved) and the checker
nudges (via `upstream_pr`) to fill in the version once it merges.
nixpkgs-pin-contains-commit:
Channel-aware, for module-level nixpkgs changes with no single package
version to gate on (e.g. a NixOS module fix). Resolved when `fix_commit`
is contained in the nixpkgs revision THIS repo pins (read from
flake.lock). `pin_node` selects the input: 'nixpkgs' (unstable) or
'nixpkgs-stable'. Gate on the channel the affected hosts actually use.
`done: true` mutes an entry once we've reverted the workaround, without
deleting the historical record.

fixes.summary: gh-dash leaks browser launcher stderr into the TUI (GTK theme warnings corrupt the display). Upstream io.Discard fix (PR #861 / commit ae6e94a, in v4.25.0) shipped but did NOT actually resolve the corruption in practice, so the local workaround has been reinstated.
fixes.workaround: features/shell/gh-dash/default.nix -- `keybindings` block overriding the `o` key with a detached/silenced opener (search FIXME(gh-dash-829)).
fixes.revert_action: BLOCKED. The obvious upstream signal (io.Discard patch ae6e94a in v4.25.0) was verified NOT to fix this in practice -- we reverted the workaround in PR #1942 / commit e385adbf and had to restore it. A `release-contains-commit` check on ae6e94a would falsely resolve immediately, so this entry is intentionally in the `pkgs-min-version` BLOCKED-by-null state (min_version=null, upstream_pr=null) and will never auto-resolve until a new signal is filed. TODO: file a new upstream issue documenting that PR #861 was insufficient, then update `tracking`, set `upstream_pr` to that new PR, and set `min_version` to the gh-dash release that actually carries the real fix. Only then revert the workaround (delete the `keybindings` block, `openDetached` helper, and `pkgs` arg from features/shell/gh-dash/default.nix), verify the TUI is clean on `o`, and set `done: true`.

fixes.summary: nixpkgs dropped `--toc-depth`/`--chunk-toc-depth` from `nixos-render-docs manual html` (use `--sidebar-depth`), but the nix-darwin pin we follow still passes the old flags, so `darwin-manual-html` fails and breaks every Darwin build on a nixpkgs bump.
fixes.workaround: profiles/darwin.nix -- BOTH `documentation.doc.enable = false;` AND `system.tools.darwin-uninstaller.enable = false;` (see FIXME(nix-darwin-1817-toc-depth)). Disabling docs alone is insufficient: the darwin-uninstaller package evaluates a second inner nix-darwin system that rebuilds the broken HTML manual with docs re-enabled, so it must be disabled too.
fixes.revert_action: DONE. Issue #1817 closed 2026-07-07; PR #1818 (`manualHTML: adopt to nixos/nixpkgs#537810`, merge commit 08920bcf) applied the `--toc-depth` -> `--sidebar-depth` swap in doc/manual/default.nix. Our `darwin` input now pins `d5bd9cd7` which is 2 commits ahead of 08920bcf and contains the fix. Removed both `documentation.doc.enable = false;` and `system.tools.darwin-uninstaller.enable = false;` (plus the FIXME block) from profiles/darwin.nix; the HTML manual and the uninstaller build again. Darwin build verification happens in ci-darwin.yaml (this repo has no local Darwin builder).

fixes.summary: opencode build-time `--version` smoke test is SIGKILLed (exit 137) on aarch64-darwin due to Mach-O page-hash code-signing corruption from the nix daemon; needs a patched daemon that has actually landed in our pinned nixpkgs.
fixes.revert_action: Once PR #15638 merges AND ships in a tagged nix release that lands in our pinned nixpkgs, set `min_version` to that nix version. When the checker then confirms pkgs.nix on a darwin-channel host is >= that version, re-enable `ai.opencode.enable = true;` and set this entry `done: true`. NOTE: eval_host is currently a Linux host (Daytona) as a placeholder for the unstable nix version; switch it to the actual darwin host attr once the carrying release is known if the darwin pin can diverge.

fixes.summary: direnv's checkPhase hangs indefinitely on darwin (fish test suite), hitting CI's 6h max with no output.
fixes.workaround: overlays/default.nix -- `direnv` overlay sets `doCheck = false` on darwin only.
fixes.revert_action: Once #507531 is fixed (issue closed) and the fix is in our pinned nixpkgs, drop the darwin branch of the `direnv` overlay so the full test suite runs again. Verify a darwin build still passes before setting `done: true`.

fixes.summary: staging-next autoconf update forced Clang to -std=gnu23, breaking dateutils 0.4.11 (dgrep.c) on aarch64-darwin.
fixes.workaround: overlays/default.nix -- `dateutils` overlay pins `CFLAGS=-std=gnu17` on darwin only.
fixes.revert_action: DONE. The umbrella issue #511329 closing was not itself the signal -- it closed once staging-next breakage was reduced enough to merge, not because dateutils was fixed. The actual fix is nixpkgs PR #526257 (merge commit 670c46f, backported to release-26.05 via #530052), which applies the upstream dateutils patch (hroptatyr b30902c) and adds flex/bison instead of the gnu17 CFLAGS hack. Verified our pinned nixpkgs (rev b5aa0fbd, which the darwin host evaluates via the nixpkgs_8 node) contains 670c46f and that pkgs.dateutils on the darwin host carries the b30902c patch + flex/bison. The patched, no-gnu17 dateutils for aarch64-darwin is already built on cache.nixos.org by upstream Hydra (store path ir1k1nb...-dateutils-0.4.11), so the from-source build is confirmed good. Overlay darwin branch removed.

fixes.summary: nixpkgs' sbomnix wrapper hard-pins nixVersions.nix_2_31 (a stale TODO from sbomnix#267), whose legacy `inputDrvs` JSON the sbomnix 1.8.0 parser refuses to consume, aborting every CVE scan with `unsupported legacy inputDrvs`.
fixes.workaround: overlays/default.nix -- `sbomnix` overlay overriding makeWrapperArgs to prepend nixVersions.nix_2_34 (emits schema version 4) instead of the upstream-pinned nix_2_31 (see FIXME(nixpkgs-sbomnix-nix231-pin)); flake/dev/packages.nix exposes it as `.#sbomnix`; cve-scan.yaml invokes `.#sbomnix` instead of `nixpkgs#sbomnix`.
fixes.revert_action: DONE. nixpkgs dropped the nix_2_31 PATH pin in df704e156dd583b8d9b6c93437785fb1f28e61bb ("sbomnix: use the latest Nix version in $PATH again", PR #538534, 2026-07-06), which is contained in our unstable pin. Verified on the file itself: the unstable pin's pkgs/by-name/sb/sbomnix/package.nix has 0 references to nix_2_31 (stable still has 1, but stable is irrelevant here -- see below). Removed ONLY the makeWrapperArgs override; the two source patches stay, since sbomnix-substituted-deriver-drop and sbomnix-pinned-version-cpe-drop are still unfixed upstream. Safety checked before removing: our wrapper and upstream's list an IDENTICAL tool set (git, nix, graphviz, nix-visualize, vulnix, grype), and `nix` and `nixVersions.nix_2_34` resolve to the byte-identical store path /nix/store/7vb637v8mqbycvmpwfl5q93ikr2xjpay-nix-2.34.8 in our pin, so dropping the override is provably a no-op. Rebuilt .#sbomnix and confirmed the wrapper still carries all six tools with nix 2.34.8 and that both patches are still applied. NOTE for the remaining sbomnix entries: `eval_host: fredhub` is misleading -- fredhub is stable, but .#sbomnix is built by flake/dev/packages.nix from the UNSTABLE nixpkgs input unconditionally, and cve-scan.yaml invokes .#sbomnix, so the unstable pin is the one that governs.

fixes.summary: sbomnix drops every runtime-closure path whose deriver `nix path-info` reports as unknown, which is every substituter-fetched path; the SBOM covered 418 of 3242 paths (13%) and silently omitted openssl, bash and glibc while keeping unit-*.service glue, so CVE scans reported near-empty results as clean successes.
fixes.workaround: overlays/default.nix -- the `sbomnix` overlay applies overlays/sbomnix-recover-substituted-derivers.patch, which reconstructs output -> deriver by inverting `outputs.<name>.path` over the local .drv graph instead of trusting the store's deriver pointers (see FIXME(sbomnix-substituted-deriver-drop)). Restores 98.9% closure coverage (408 -> 2835 components on Daytona). cve-scan.yaml additionally asserts >= 60% coverage so a future regression fails loudly instead of silently reporting an empty scan.
fixes.revert_action: No upstream issue is filed yet, so `min_version: null` keeps this BLOCKED (never falsely resolved) as a manual re-check reminder. File an upstream issue against tiiuae/sbomnix describing the substituted-deriver drop, then retarget this entry to `issue-closed` (or to `pkgs-min-version` once a carrying sbomnix release is known). To revert: confirm the pinned sbomnix recovers derivers itself by running sbomnix against a flakeref and checking the component count is within ~15% of `nix path-info --recursive <out> | wc -l`; then delete overlays/sbomnix-recover-substituted-derivers.patch, drop the `patches` attribute from the sbomnix overlay along with its FIXME, confirm a manual `workflow_dispatch` CVE scan is green and the coverage assertion still passes, then set `done: true`. Keep the coverage assertion in cve-scan.yaml regardless -- it guards the class of bug, not this instance.

fixes.summary: sbomnix matches nixpkgs metadata to components only by exact output/derivation path, so a closure pinning a different version than the nixpkgs attribute currently builds gets no metadata and therefore no CPE; such components are invisible to grype and report as clean. Servers pinning linux 6.18.41 while pkgs.linux was 6.18.43 scored ZERO kernel CVEs while a version-matching desktop scored 74, and only 59 of 1819 components fleet-wide carried a CPE.
fixes.workaround: overlays/default.nix -- the `sbomnix` overlay applies overlays/sbomnix-recover-pinned-version-cpes.patch, adding a lowest-priority pname fallback in match_package_metadata_to_components() that carries over only the CPE, plus _retarget_cpe_version() in builder.py which rewrites the CPE version to the version actually present in the closure, strips nixpkgs-only revision suffixes (glibc 2.42-67 -> 2.42) and preserves an accurate CPE version/update split (bash 5.3p9 = version 5.3, update 9). See FIXME(sbomnix-pinned-version-cpe-drop). cve-scan.yaml additionally asserts a floor on the number of components carrying a CPE so a future regression fails loudly.
fixes.revert_action: No upstream issue is filed yet, so `min_version: null` keeps this BLOCKED (never falsely resolved) as a manual re-check reminder. File an upstream issue against tiiuae/sbomnix describing the path-only metadata match, then retarget this entry to `issue-closed` or to `pkgs-min-version` once a carrying release is known. To revert: run the pinned sbomnix against a host whose kernel version differs from `pkgs.linux` and confirm the emitted `linux` component carries a cpe matching the CLOSURE's version, not the attribute's; then delete overlays/sbomnix-recover-pinned-version-cpes.patch, drop it from the `patches` list along with its FIXME, confirm a manual workflow_dispatch CVE scan is green and the scannable-component assertion still passes, then set `done: true`. Keep that assertion regardless -- it guards the class of bug, not this instance.

fixes.summary: nixpkgs' classic ld64 (cctools-binutils-darwin-1010.6) crashes in its stubs pass with `Trace/BPT trap: 5` when linking any Rust binary that pulls `mac-notification-sys` via `notify-rust`. This kills the aarch64-darwin build of freminal 0.11.1 (and previously killed cargo-watch, since removed).
fixes.workaround: features/desktop/freminal/default.nix -- darwin-only `overrideAttrs` on the freminal flake package adding `llvmPackages.lld` to nativeBuildInputs and setting `env.NIX_CFLAGS_LINK = "-fuse-ld=lld"` (see FIXME(nixpkgs-536365-ld64-mac-notification-sys)). Mirrors the per-package hotfix nixpkgs applied to starship in PR #540463.
fixes.revert_action: DONE. #536365 ("ld64: disable hardening again") merged 2026-07-15 as 24de2af2c1c94772a72daa9abe6cef9cbcb0a49c; the all-zero fix_commit placeholder is replaced with it. Contained in the unstable pin (compare reports `behind`) and NOT in the stable pin (`diverged`) -- which is correct and sufficient, because the Darwin hosts evaluate the unstable nixpkgs (verified: darwinConfigurations pkgs.lib.version = 26.11pre-git) and the override was gated darwin-only, so no server ever carried it. Verified beyond merge status: the pinned ld64/package.nix carries `hardeningDisable = [ "libcxxhardeningfast" ]`, and upstream DELETED its own equivalent starship lld hack in the same commit (0 matches for `fuse-ld=lld` in the pinned starship recipe) -- i.e. upstream considers the root fix sufficient to drop the identical workaround we were mirroring. Removed the overrideAttrs block from features/desktop/freminal/default.nix (and the now-unused `pkgs` module argument, which deadnix caught). Darwin toplevels evaluate clean locally; the actual freminal BUILD is verified by ci-darwin.yaml, as there is no local Darwin builder.
fixes.$comment: The upstream conversation on issue #540450 identifies #536365 as the root fix; #540463 is the starship-only hotfix we cargo-cult here for freminal.

fixes.summary: nixpkgs bumped pandas to 3.0.4 but df-diskcache still pins `pandas<3` in its v0.1.0 requirements, so the pythonRuntimeDepsCheckHook aborts the dfdiskcache build; this transitively breaks sbomnix (which depends on dfdiskcache), taking out the weekly CVE scan and the `.#sbomnix` dev-shell package.
fixes.workaround: overlays/default.nix -- `pythonPackagesExtensions` block that appends `pandas` to `dfdiskcache`'s `pythonRelaxDeps` (see FIXME(nixpkgs-540439-dfdiskcache-pandas3)). Applies globally since the overlay is imported by both mk-system.nix and flake/dev/packages.nix, so both `nixosConfigurations.*.pkgs.sbomnix` and the standalone `.#sbomnix` package build.
fixes.revert_action: DONE. PR #540439 merged 2026-07-21 as 9699a4042d6c963fb5b4e63d41cde65b3dd2b00f and is contained in our unstable pin. Verified on the file rather than on merge status: dfdiskcache/default.nix in the unstable pin carries `pythonRelaxDeps` (1 match) and the stable pin does not (0 matches). Stable is irrelevant here: dfdiskcache is only ever built as a transitive dep of .#sbomnix, which flake/dev/packages.nix builds from the UNSTABLE nixpkgs input, and neither sbomnix nor dfdiskcache appears in any host's systemPackages (checked fredhub, sdrhub, Daytona). Removed the pythonPackagesExtensions block from overlays/default.nix; .#sbomnix rebuilt green afterwards. Upstream df-diskcache still hard-pins pandas<3 on master, so the nixpkgs-side pythonRelaxDeps must remain a nixpkgs concern -- that is expected, not a regression.
fixes.$comment: `package` is `python3Packages.dfdiskcache` for diagnostic purposes only; the null `min_version` means pkg_version_in_pin is never actually evaluated against a target.

fixes.summary: fwupd-refresh.service fails with 'Failed to obtain auth' on every timer fire because the fwupd-refresh user has no seat; we grant the refresh polkit actions by username instead.
fixes.workaround: features/common/system/default.nix -- second `polkit.addRule` block granting fwupd refresh actions to the fwupd-refresh user (see the comment referencing NixOS/nixpkgs#526476).
fixes.revert_action: DONE. Removed the fwupd-refresh polkit block from features/common/system/default.nix. The `pin_node: nixpkgs` gate was NOT sufficient on its own and would have been unsafe to act on blindly: this workaround lives in features/common/system, which applies to every Linux host, so the eight stable-channel servers needed the fix too. The recorded fix_commit 5ec8276a (master, 2026-06-06 18:50) is genuinely absent from the stable pin -- `compare` reports `diverged` -- because it was backported to release-26.05 as a DIFFERENT sha, 110912079417 (2026-06-06 18:51), which the stable pin does contain. Verified on ground truth rather than topology: the `security.polkit.extraConfig` block in nixos/modules/services/hardware/fwupd.nix is byte-identical to ours in BOTH pinned channels, and the rule count in the evaluated config went from 2 (ours + upstream's) to 1 on sdrhub, fredvps and maranello -- i.e. the rule is retained, only the duplicate is gone.

fixes.summary: Vicinae (our app launcher) fails to resolve the freedesktop icon name "printer" via QIcon::fromTheme, showing a "?" placeholder for system-config-printer's launcher entry, even though the exact same icon theme resolves every other icon we tested (including other printing-related ones like `cups`) and a standalone QIcon::fromTheme("printer") call succeeds outside of vicinae. Confirmed live on maranello: neither a valid icon theme name nor "auto" changes the outcome, ruling out theme/config causes.
fixes.workaround: features/desktop/print/default.nix -- `system-config-printer-iconfix` overrides system-config-printer's .desktop `Icon=printer` to an absolute path pointing at the package's own bundled `i-network-printer.png`, bypassing icon-theme-name resolution entirely (see FIXME(vicinae-468-printer-icon)).
fixes.revert_action: No upstream PR/issue exists yet for this specific "printer" name bug (only the linked discussion, where multiple reporters hit the identical symptom, unresolved as of Oct 2025) so `min_version` stays null (BLOCKED) until one is filed and a fix version is known. Once vicinae ships a fix and our pinned nixpkgs' `vicinae` package version reflects it, set `min_version` accordingly (or `done: true` after manually confirming `Icon=printer` renders correctly in vicinae), then delete `system-config-printer-iconfix` and its FIXME from features/desktop/print/default.nix, reverting to a plain `programs.system-config-printer.enable = true;`.
fixes.$comment: No upstream_pr recorded yet -- if one is opened for this specific bug, add its number here so the checker nudges once merged.

fixes.summary: attic's orphan-chunk reaper deletes at most 500 chunks per GC pass on SQLite and does not loop, so a cache producing more orphans per day than 500 x passes/day can never converge. The 500 cites SQLite's pre-3.32 999-variable limit; the SQLite compiled into the binary reports MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER=32766.
fixes.workaround: overlays/attic-server.nix -- postPatch substituteInPlace raising `DatabaseBackend::Sqlite => 500` to 10000 (see FIXME(attic-gc-sqlite-chunk-limit)); wired in overlays/default.nix. Paired with a 15-minute garbage-collection interval in modules/services/attic/attic_server.nix.
fixes.revert_action: NOT YET REPORTED UPSTREAM -- file an issue/PR against zhaofengli/attic first (either raise the SQLite limit or make run_reap_orphan_chunks loop until drained), then set `upstream_pr` and add the issue URL to `tracking`. Once a fix ships and lands in our pinned nixpkgs, set `min_version` to the carrying attic-server version; when the checker confirms it, delete overlays/attic-server.nix, its entry in overlays/default.nix and the FIXME, rebuild fredhub, and set this entry `done: true`. min_version is null so this entry stays BLOCKED and can never falsely resolve.

fixes.summary: OBSOLETE, not fixed upstream. Frigate 0.17.2's OpenVINO detector still cannot use YOLOX models (openvino.py's yolox branch builds a 7-column array, then assigns the 6-element result of process_yolo() into its rows and returns it to a caller expecting (20, 6)). nvrhub no longer cares: it runs the `onnx` detector on CUDA with YOLOv9, so the OpenVINO plugin is not in the path at all. The workaround this entry tracked -- falling back to the tflite `cpu` detector -- is gone, so there is nothing left to revert and nothing to wait for.
fixes.workaround: REMOVED. hosts/linux/nvrhub/frigate.nix now uses detectors.onnx1 (type = onnx) with YOLOv9-s at 640x640, built by hosts/linux/nvrhub/frigate-model.nix and running on CUDAExecutionProvider via the onnxruntime override in hosts/linux/nvrhub/cuda-onnxruntime.nix. The FIXME(frigate-openvino-yolox-detection-shape) comment has been deleted along with the cpu-detector block.
fixes.revert_action: None. Closed by changing approach rather than by an upstream fix, so this entry is marked done to keep the historical record rather than because the bug was resolved. NOTE for anyone reading the old text: it claimed a yolox derivation 'was deleted as hosts/linux/nvrhub/frigate-model.nix and must be restored from git history'. That file was never committed -- verified across all history -- so nothing was recoverable. The frigate-model.nix that exists today is a new YOLOv9 derivation, unrelated to that claim. If OpenVINO/YOLOX is ever wanted again, it must be written from scratch.

fixes.summary: rust-overlay lib/mk-aggregated.nix uses the deprecated stdenv.isLinux / stdenv.isDarwin aliases (lines 76, 85, 97). Unstable nixpkgs now wraps those aliases in lib.warn (pkgs/stdenv/generic/default.nix, "Added 2026-05-09"), and our CI fails on any `evaluation warning:`. freminal and frext each instantiate their own pkgs, so each contributes one isLinux + one isDarwin warning to desktop and Darwin builds. Neither repo can fix this itself -- the call sites are in rust-overlay, which both consume for their Rust toolchain.
fixes.workaround: flake.nix -- both the `freminal` and `frext` inputs override `inputs.rust-overlay.url` to the PR head commit on the author's fork, github:K900/rust-overlay/2c2d808349ea4e8ba3823b3ad23151b5b0328f75 (see FIXME(rust-overlay-262)). Pinned to the commit rather than the `hostplatform` branch so a force-push cannot change what we build. The PR is a 3-line pure rename with no semantic change.
fixes.revert_action: DONE. PR #262 merged 2026-08-13T16:24:02Z as merge commit 892c035d7c2ff75acd5da10424a47ab454e1f3dc. freminal, frext and github-ci-exporter have each bumped their own rust-overlay pin, and all seven rust-overlay nodes in our flake.lock now resolve to 892c035d, so the fix is present without any override. All three `inputs.rust-overlay.url` overrides and their FIXME comments were removed from flake.nix. Verified: Daytona toplevel and sdrhub home-manager activationPackage both evaluate with exit 0 and zero warnings.

fixes.summary: nixpkgs marks ladybird-0-unstable-2026-06-05 as insecure (CVE-2026-58592), which is a hard evaluation failure on both desktops because profiles/desktop enables ladybird by default. Ladybird is an experimental browser and the package in our pin has no patched successor yet.
fixes.workaround: features/desktop/default.nix -- `ladybird.enable = false;` (see FIXME(nixpkgs-ladybird-cve-2026-58592)). Deliberately NOT added to `permittedInsecurePackages` in features/common/system/default.nix: that list is now empty (the openssl-1.1.1w entry it used to hold was removed once nothing in the fleet needed it), and ladybird is a browser, so its vulnerability is reachable from untrusted network input rather than being a transitive library concern.
fixes.revert_action: Once nixpkgs ships a ladybird build that is no longer flagged insecure, set `min_version` to that version so the checker can resolve. Then set `ladybird.enable = true;` in features/desktop/default.nix, delete the FIXME, confirm a desktop toplevel evaluates without NIXPKGS_ALLOW_INSECURE, and set `done: true`. min_version is null so this entry stays BLOCKED and cannot falsely resolve.

fixes.summary: dwarfs 0.14.0 fails to compile in the current nixpkgs. Its bundled folly-lite copy calls std::memset without including <cstring>, which the current GCC rejects ("error: memset is not a member of std; did you mean wmemset?" in folly/portability/Unistd.cpp, SysUio.cpp, io/IOBufQueue.cpp and json/dynamic.cpp). dwarfs is a build dependency of gearlever, so both desktops failed to build. Upstream fix is the 0.15.6 bump in NixOS/nixpkgs#549694.
fixes.workaround: features/desktop/appimage/default.nix -- `gearlever` commented out of the per-user package list (see FIXME(nixpkgs-549694-dwarfs-gcc)). Deliberately scoped to gearlever alone: appimage-run and the boot.binfmt.registrations.appimage block in the same file are what actually provide AppImage support, and neither depends on dwarfs, so running AppImages still works. Only the GUI manager is gone.
fixes.revert_action: DONE. #549694 merged 2026-08-28 as d7e1d8887d64 (dwarfs 0.14.0 -> 0.15.7, one patch above the 0.15.6 the issue asked for) and closed #549542; our unstable pin 83199d0d evaluates dwarfs at 0.15.7. gearlever is uncommented in features/desktop/appimage/default.nix and the FIXME is gone. Verified by BUILDING, not evaluating, because this was a compile failure: `dwarfs` 0.15.7 and `gearlever` 3.4.7 both realise from cache.nixos.org (so Hydra compiled them), and both desktop toplevels -- maranello and Daytona, the recorded eval_host -- build green with exactly one gearlever path in the closure. Scope note: gearlever is desktop-only, so only the unstable pin was ever relevant here.

fixes.summary: switch-to-configuration stops the network daemon and then daemon-reexecs PID 1 (which it does whenever systemd's store path moves -- a glibc/stdenv mass rebuild is enough, the version need not change). On re-exec systemd-fstab-generator stat()s our `hard` NFS mounts with no network, blocks forever, the generator sandbox times out after 90s, safe_fork(FORK_WAIT) reports -EPROTO, and PID 1 executes `Freezing execution.` -- alive but deaf to D-Bus, so nothing starts or stops and `reboot` hangs too. Needs SysRq or a power cycle. Observed on maranello 2026-08-29 20:21:59 and repeatedly on Daytona.
fixes.workaround: Three parts, all keyed to FIXME(nixpkgs-375376-stc-network-freeze). (1) features/common/system/default.nix sets `systemd.services.NetworkManager.reloadIfChanged = true`, so activation reloads NetworkManager instead of restarting it and the network survives the re-exec. (2) scripts/switch-preflight.sh refuses a live switch (exit 10) when dry-activate reports `would restart systemd` AND live NFS/CIFS mounts exist AND the network is going away under them (a watched unit is in the stop/restart set, or the fileserver is already unreachable); it also reports units left running a superseded binary as a consequence of (1). Wired into `updatenix` in dotfiles/shell/40-functions.sh, which falls back to `nixos-rebuild boot` + reboot. (3) scripts/colmena-apply-drifted.sh refuses to switch remote nodes whose deploy moves systemd's store path while they have network filesystems mounted, since recovering a frozen remote node means physically visiting it.
